design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (shopper_batch_pay_and_tips, category batch).

[1] Why this is a good test. The shopper (Nadia Pereira, Full-Service Shopper Gold) only says her Triple Delivery Batch at Market Basket, Somerville Ave paid $33.15 against an offer of $42.40. The real support capability forced out: read the batch's earnings ledger against the pay rules, notice two ledger defects the shopper never mentions (the mileage component posted twice on 2026-03-17 and the long-distance bonus never posted although the 13.6-mile estimated route exceeds the threshold), correct both at their own multi-factor amounts, hand the shopper the dispute filing with a claimed shortfall that is only defined on the corrected ledger, then approve the adjustment from that claim. Difficulty comes from reading prerequisite sentences, reconciling the batch ledger (7 pay rows) plus shopper and payout records, and arithmetic with 18 declared factors; no information is missing and there is exactly one tool per problem.

[2] Scope snapshot. Occupied before this task: nothing (task 0). Claimed here: batch_ext_long_distance_bonus, batch_ext_duplicate_recovery, batch_ext_shown_pay_claim, batch_ext_shown_pay_adjustment with tools post_pay_component_6b97a1a8, reverse_duplicate_pay_33b66c45, submit_pay_dispute_0c2b2ed2 (owner user), book_pay_adjustment_e97659e1. Left for task 1 (draw: 2 prerequisites, factor counts [4,4,5]): the completed-batch mileage flow — batch_ext_undelivered_recovery (a reversal on the verified not-delivered ground against the batch's mileage posting when a wrong-address violation is recorded against the batch), batch_ext_mileage_claim (the shopper's own mileage dispute) and batch_ext_mileage_adjustment, on reverse_undelivered_pay_ec14645c, submit_mileage_claim_29030431 (owner user) and book_mileage_adjustment_6fe9f3bb. Neither flow's policies, tools or root overlap the other. (Revision round 2: this paragraph previously named a canceled-batch plan for task 1 and two tools that were never written; corrected per audit T0-2.)

[3] Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py <diff> --task 0): {"task": 0, "key": "env_0027_grocery_delivery_platform/shopper_batch_pay_and_tips/0", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [4, 5, 5, 4]}. Assignment: batch_ext_long_distance_bonus 5 factors, batch_ext_shown_pay_claim 5, batch_ext_duplicate_recovery 4, batch_ext_shown_pay_adjustment 4 (multiset {4,4,5,5} = draw).

[4] Problem-tree card. Root = batch_ext_shown_pay_adjustment (the customer's surface request: be paid what the offer promised). Edges:
 (a) shown_pay_adjustment -> shown_pay_claim, kind value_input, gate sa_claim, form state, prerequisite sentence: "A shown-pay adjustment is booked only after the batch carries a submitted shown-pay shortfall dispute from the shopper stating a claimed amount." Condition: batch_pay_disputes has a submitted shown_pay_shortfall row for the batch. False at opening: initial_state has no batch_pay_disputes table at all (find_batch_pay_disputes on the batch returns nothing). Resolved by submit_pay_dispute_0c2b2ed2 (owner user). Deletion sensitivity: skipping the filing makes the adjustment compute 0 (sa_claims = 0) instead of 6.58, and the dispute row plus the approved status disappear from the terminal DB.
 (b) shown_pay_claim -> long_distance_bonus, kind value_input, gate sc_posted, form state, sentence: "The claimed shortfall is fixed only after the batch's earnings entries carry a long-distance bonus whenever the estimated route exceeds the long-distance threshold that applies to the shopper." False at opening: the batch's seven batch_pay_posted rows carry pay_component batch_base, per_order, mileage, mileage, wait_time, peak_boost, quality_bonus — no long_distance — while batches.estimated_miles = 13.6 exceeds the 8.0-mile threshold that applies to a Gold account 57 months past activation (and even the type threshold of 10.0). Resolved by post_pay_component_6b97a1a8. Skipping it: claim 8.28 instead of 4.10.
 (c) shown_pay_claim -> duplicate_recovery, kind value_input, gate sc_reversed, form state, sentence: "The claimed shortfall is not worked out until every mileage posting that stands twice on the batch carries a reversal against its later posting." False at opening: two mileage rows of 6.30, dated 2026-03-17 and 2026-03-18, and no batch_pay_reversed row. Resolved by reverse_duplicate_pay_33b66c45. Skipping it: claim 1.65 instead of 4.10.
 Four-point test on each sentence: (1) ordering connective "only after" (a, b, affirmative) and "not ... until" (c, negated; contrapositive of "worked out only after every duplicated mileage posting carries a reversal"); (2) the waited-on side is a record-visible state (a submitted dispute on the batch; a long-distance bonus entry on the earnings entries; a reversal entry against the later mileage posting) — no action or performer named; (3) no tool, policy id or snake_case token; (4) strength: hard requirement, scope exactly the edge condition. Exactly one write of this difficulty brings each state about: only the shopper's dispute filing creates a shown_pay_shortfall dispute; only the component posting writes a long_distance posting (no other policy posts components); only the duplicate recovery writes a reversal against the later of two mileage postings. The other reversal policy of the difficulty (batch_ext_undelivered_recovery) also acts on completed batches and also books against a mileage posting, but on the verified not-delivered ground and only where a wrong-address violation is recorded against the batch; this batch carries no wrong-address violation (its only violation is a late delivery), so that policy owes nothing here and cannot be the write the sentence waits on, which names the posting that stands twice. At the tool layer the not-delivered tool could mechanically name the later mileage posting; the rules single out the duplicate recovery by its trigger and its ground. Derivation: sentence + records (no long_distance row, 13.6 > 8.0; two mileage rows, no reversal; no dispute) + each depended-on rule's opening sentence ("A long-distance bonus that is due ... is posted by the desk"; "the desk takes it back with one reversal"; "disputes it herself by submitting a shown-pay shortfall dispute") -> exactly one resolving action per edge. Directions: the charter uses both (claim edge (c) negated; (a), (b) affirmative), chosen as the desk would say each wait.
 Topological order: long_distance_bonus and duplicate_recovery (either order) -> shown_pay_claim -> shown_pay_adjustment. Parallel edges (b), (c): the bonus computation reads no reversal and no mileage row other than per-order pay; the recovery reads only mileage postings, shopper and payout records; replaying the gold with the two writes swapped gives the identical terminal DB (checked: swap same terminal: True) and both values unchanged (2.45 and 4.18).
 user_scenario names no prerequisite: it never mentions a duplicate, a reversal, a long-distance bonus or a dispute; the shopper only reacts after the agent says so. Tools block nothing: every task-tool body is one ctx.create plus updates with no condition on existing rows (task_tools.py).

[5] Factor card (handling-time world; figure = result with that factor alone at its baseline). Revision round 3 (audit N1) rebuilt the long-distance route extension and set the shown-pay rating approval share's upper tier to 1.04; every figure below comes from the round-3 run and was checked in exact decimal half-up arithmetic (no half-cent tie).
 batch_ext_long_distance_bonus = 4.18 on the opening world (step 10).
  - ld_threshold_by_standing (parameter, cross shopper, multi-source): level_min_batches_30d 80 (Gold) AND MONTHS(2021-06-14, 2026-03-18) = 57 >= 36 -> 8.0 miles; baseline type threshold 10.0 -> 3.96 (the late-tier extension shrinks to 0.10 x 3 whole miles = 0.30).
  - ld_amount_by_points (parameter, cross shopper): violation_points_balance 1 -> type bonus 2.00 + 0.50 = 2.50; baseline type bonus 2.00 -> 3.63.
  - ld_route_extension (method, cross shopper, multi-source): route excess 13.6 - 10.0 = 3.6 >= 3.0 AND one late_delivery violation against the batch -> 0.10 for each whole estimated mile beyond 8.0: 5 whole miles -> 0.50. The on-time tier would instead grow the bonus proportionally, 2.50 x 5.6 / 8.0 = 1.75 -> 1.70 (a 5.50 bonus for the same shopper on time), so the late tier always pays less: with a route excess of 3 miles or more, the proportional tier yields at least 0.20 per mile on every batch type (type bonus / type threshold is 2.00/10 or 3.00/15, and the tiers only raise the amount or lower the threshold). Baseline flat bonus only -> 3.63.
  - ld_order_supplement (parameter, history): per-order pay 6.00 / 3.00 = 2 additional orders -> 0.40 x 2 = 0.80; baseline 0 -> 3.30.
  - ld_card_uplift (parameter, cross payout): Everyday Pay Card Gold (fuel cashback 3.0) -> 1.10; baseline 1.00 -> 3.80.
  (2.50 + 0.50 + 0.80) x 1.10 = 4.18. All factors at baseline: flat 2.00. Near-miss: actual_miles 14.2 (GPS) is never the distance compared (it would give 6 whole miles, 0.60).
 batch_ext_duplicate_recovery = 2.45 (step 12, opening world).
  - dr_loyalty_allowance (parameter, cross shopper, multi-source): Gold AND 57 months -> 1.00; baseline 0 -> 2.95.
  - dr_standing_allowance (parameter, cross shopper, multi-source): 1 active point AND 1 late-delivery violation on the batch -> 0.25; baseline 0 -> 2.57.
  - dr_same_day_allowance (parameter, history): first mileage posting dated 2026-03-17 = completed_date, the second 2026-03-18, so exactly one is dated the completion date -> 0.15; baseline 0 -> 2.52.
  - dr_cashout_method (method, cross payout): instant cashout 25.00 on 2026-03-17 (less than a month before) AND Everyday Pay Card plan -> remainder halved and rounded down; baseline taken in full -> 4.90.
  6.30 - 1.00 - 0.25 - 0.15 = 4.90 -> halved 2.45. All at baseline: 6.30. Near-miss: the two mileage rows carry the same amount; only the posting dates tell which is the later one.
 batch_ext_shown_pay_claim = 4.10 (step 14, after the bonus 4.18 and the reversal 2.45 are booked).
  - sc_late_order_guarantee (method, cross shopper): one late-delivery violation on a 3-order batch -> 42.40 - 3.00 = 39.40; baseline shown pay whole -> 7.01.
  - sc_standing_share (parameter, cross shopper): 1 active point -> 0.97; baseline 1.00 -> 5.28.
  - sc_offer_tolerance (parameter, cross shopper, multi-source): Gold AND 57 months -> 0; baseline 0.50 -> 3.60.
  - sc_waiting_offset (parameter, history): waiting-time pay posted 1.05 -> 0.75 of it set against the offer; baseline all -> 3.84.
  - sc_five_star_supplement (parameter, cross shopper): one five-star rating on the batch -> 0.50; baseline 0 -> 3.60.
  Pay standing 37.33 posted - 2.45 reversed = 34.88; counted 34.88 - 1.05 x 0.25 = 34.6175; 39.40 x 0.97 + 0.50 - 34.6175 - 0 = 4.1005 -> 4.10. All at baseline: 42.40 - 34.88 - 0.50 = 7.02. Near-miss: the 4-star rating is not a five-star rating.
 batch_ext_shown_pay_adjustment = 6.58 (step 16).
  - sa_rating_approval_share (parameter, cross shopper, multi-source): two ratings (5 and 4), none of three stars or fewer -> 1.04; baseline 1.00 -> 6.41.
  - sa_makegood_credit (parameter, cross shopper, multi-source): Gold AND 57 months -> 1.50; baseline 0 -> 5.01.
  - sa_prompt_credit (parameter, date): DAYS(2026-03-17, 2026-03-18) = 1 -> 0.50; baseline 0 -> 6.06.
  - sa_card_method (method, cross payout): Everyday Pay Card Gold -> sum x 1.05 rounded up; baseline sum as is -> 6.26.
  4.10 x 1.04 + 1.50 + 0.50 = 6.264; x 1.05 = 6.5772 -> rounded up 6.58. All at baseline: 4.10.
 Per task: multi-source factors include ld_route_extension, dr_standing_allowance, dr_cashout_method and sc_late_order_guarantee, besides the level-and-tenure ladders; cross-difficulty factors 14 (shopper and payout records seeded for this shopper).
 No second product law: every factor refines an existing base pay mechanism; the base sentences whose outcome differs are declared in overwrite.

[6] Base-invariant card.
 Step 10 (batch_pay_posted, long_distance): batch_evt_pay_calculation.payable_state — "Components are posted only on a batch that is completed or canceled, never on a dropped one." evidence batches.status = completed (initial_state); once_per_component — no long_distance row on the batch.
 Step 12 (batch_pay_reversed): batch_evt_clawback.clawback_window — completed_date 2026-03-17 is day 0, last day 2026-04-16 inclusive; frozen 2026-03-18 is day 1 (inside). Just-before/at-boundary: 2026-04-16 still reversible, 2026-04-17 not. reverse_once — no reversal names the second mileage row; ground duplicate_pay is in the Triple Delivery Batch clawback_reasons.
 Step 14 (dispute filing, subject batch_completed): batch_evt_pay_calculation and batch_evt_lifecycle carry no eligibility for batch_completed (policy_scope).
 Step 16 (batch_pay_adjusted): batch_agg_adjustment_limits.within_agent_limits — no batch_pay_adjusted row for this shopper in the 30 days to 2026-03-18 (0 < 3) and 6.58 <= Triple cap 25.00; batch_evt_pay_disputes.dispute_window — completed 2026-03-17 day 0, last day 2026-03-24 inclusive, dispute filed 2026-03-18 (day 1); boundary: 2026-03-24 accepted, 2026-03-25 not; one_per_reason — no shown_pay_shortfall adjustment exists on the batch. Orders unchanged after acceptance is the caller's statement ("all three orders stayed exactly as they were offered"). The batch is still completed (not finalized): it completed on the evening of 2026-03-17 and the Triple type finalizes 24 hours after completion, after frozen_time 2026-03-18 10:40.

[7] Business-object card. Target object: batch B0 (Triple Delivery Batch, Market Basket, Somerville Ave, accepted 2026-03-17T15:52:00). Rows included: the seven batch_pay_posted rows (all batch-level, order_id empty); the duplicate is the later mileage row (6.30, posted 2026-03-18); the reversal carries it as source_event_id. The dispute is keyed to batch_id B0 and the adjustment carries its batch_pay_dispute_id. Shopper events rows all carry batch_id B0; payout credits carry batch_event_id links to each pay row; the instant cashout (25.00) is the only payout debit. No other batch exists for the shopper, so nothing on another batch can be confused with this one.

[8] Why each seed row exists. customers (identity: phone, DOB, email); shopper_accounts (level Gold, activated 2021-06-14, 1 active point: threshold, tolerance, allowance, make-good, standing share); shopper_events (late_delivery violation on B0: route extension, standing allowance, guarantee method; ratings 5 and 4: five-star supplement and rating approval share); payout_accounts (Everyday Pay Card Gold: card uplift, cash-out method, card method); payout_events (seven earnings credits mirroring the batch rows as their triggers require, and the 2026-03-17 instant cashout of 25.00 that selects the halving method); batches (route, waiting, shown pay, status, dates); batch_events (the seven pay rows; the duplicate and the missing bonus are the problems). Removing the later mileage row removes edge (c); adding a long_distance row removes edge (b). Automatic clauses: the Triple batch finalizes 24 h after completion (not yet reached); ratings within the window earn a quality bonus (the one five-star rating has its 0.50 posted); the violation expires after 90 days (active). No cache is used as a trap: earnings_usd 33.15 equals the ledger and available_balance_usd 8.15 equals credits 33.15 minus the 25.00 cashout.

[9] Persona design. A practical, slightly irritated Gold shopper. Volunteers only the surface goal and the two figures she sees (42.40 offer, 33.15 pay, both in initial_state). Gives phone to locate, DOB then email to verify; describes the batch in plain words when asked; answers "orders unchanged" and "last drop-off late" only when asked; states her own naive 9.25 difference as a trap that the policy excludes; reacts passively to the reversal and the bonus; files the dispute with the reason and amount the agent gives her; closes when told the adjustment is credited. She raises no other ask.

[10] Where a careless agent goes wrong. (i) Computing the claim straight from the opening ledger — the prerequisite sentences forbid it; the result would be 8.28 without the bonus, 1.65 without the reversal. (ii) Filing the shopper's own 9.25 as the claim. (iii) Measuring distance on driven miles (14.2) for the bonus. (iv) Applying the proportional extension of the on-time tier although a late delivery is recorded (bonus 5.50), or counting the part mile (0.56). (v) Reversing the whole 6.30 (baseline) instead of applying the three allowances and the card cash-out halving. (vi) Reversing the earlier mileage row: the rule names the later posting (2026-03-18). (vii) Treating the 4-star rating as five-star, or forgetting that waiting pay is only three-quarters set against the offer. (viii) Rounding the card method to the nearest cent (6.58 happens to agree here only because 6.5772 rounds up either way; the rule says up). (ix) Booking the adjustment without a filed dispute. Each is excluded by a rule sentence quoted in the tracing.

[11] Standard solution. Locate by phone 6175541382 -> verify with phone + DOB 1990-04-17 -> read shopper account, batches, batch earnings entries, pay disputes (none), shopper events, payout account, payout events. Write in topological order: post long_distance 4.18 (post_pay_component_6b97a1a8, order_id ""), reverse 2.45 against the 2026-03-18 mileage posting (reverse_duplicate_pay_33b66c45) — these two commute — then unlock submit_pay_dispute_0c2b2ed2 and hand it over: the shopper files shown_pay_shortfall 4.10 and reads back the dispute reference, then book_pay_adjustment_e97659e1 credits 6.58 against that dispute (reason shown_pay_shortfall) and marks it approved. Terminal: batch earnings 33.15 + 4.18 - 2.45 + 6.58 = 41.46.

[12] Verification (executed, revision round 3). A scratch evaluator imports check_compute (build_env, eval_compute, substitute), replays the gold writes with the real share and task tools on DB.seeded(initial_state), evaluates each policy just before its own step, and re-evaluates every figure with an exact decimal half-up RND to catch half-cent ties. Output:
 batch_ext_long_distance_bonus 4.18 (exact 4.18) {ld_threshold_by_standing: 3.96, ld_amount_by_points: 3.63, ld_route_extension: 3.63, ld_order_supplement: 3.3, ld_card_uplift: 3.8, all: 2.0}
 batch_ext_duplicate_recovery 2.45 (exact 2.45) {dr_loyalty_allowance: 2.95, dr_standing_allowance: 2.57, dr_same_day_allowance: 2.52, dr_cashout_method: 4.9, all: 6.3}
 batch_ext_shown_pay_claim 4.10 (exact 4.10) {sc_late_order_guarantee: 7.01, sc_standing_share: 5.28, sc_offer_tolerance: 3.6, sc_waiting_offset: 3.84, sc_five_star_supplement: 3.6, all: 7.02}
 batch_ext_shown_pay_adjustment 6.58 (exact 6.58) {sa_rating_approval_share: 6.41, sa_makegood_credit: 5.01, sa_prompt_credit: 6.06, sa_card_method: 6.26, all: 4.1}
 no tie between float and exact decimal on any figure; claim skip LD 8.28 | skip DR 1.65 | adjustment skip SC 0 | swap LD/DR same terminal | terminal earnings 41.46 | counterfactual: the same shopper with no late-delivery violation would get a 5.50 bonus (on-time tier).
 Revision log: (1) round 1: ceil written as -int(-x) was a floor -> -(-x // 1). (2) round 1: the two mileage postings first shared one date -> the re-post is dated 2026-03-18. (3) round 2 (audit F1, F4, T0-2): LD extension and amount ladders rebuilt; rationale [2] and [4] corrected about the sibling task. (4) round 3 (audit N1): the round-2 late tier outpaid the on-time tier; the on-time tier is now the proportional extension and the late tier 0.10 per whole mile; SA's upper rating tier 1.05 -> 1.04 because the new claim (4.10) put the card-method fall-back on a half cent; all values recomputed (LD 4.18, claim 4.10, adjustment 6.58; DR unchanged 2.45).

[13] Closure. long_distance_bonus -> post_pay_component_6b97a1a8 -> 10/amount_usd -> long_distance posting 4.18; duplicate_recovery -> reverse_duplicate_pay_33b66c45 -> 12/amount_usd -> reversal 2.45; shown_pay_claim -> submit_pay_dispute_0c2b2ed2 -> 14/claimed_amount_usd -> dispute submitted 4.10; shown_pay_adjustment -> book_pay_adjustment_e97659e1 -> 16/amount_usd -> adjustment 6.58 and dispute approved. charter_scope = required_documents = computations' policy ids = the tree. No obligation is left open. No handoff.

[14] Solvability vs GT and a draft recomputation from visible context. Every write's base preconditions cite initial_state rows or prior steps (see solvability_contract). Masked recomputation: from the rules as they will be published, the tool schemas, the share-tool returns and the persona lines only, the reader finds the adjustment waits on a submitted dispute, the claim waits on the bonus and on the duplicate's reversal, reads every figure from the lookups (Gold, activation 2021-06-14, 1 point, one late-delivery violation and ratings 5 and 4 on the batch, Everyday Pay Card Gold, cashout 25.00 on 2026-03-17, the seven pay rows) and reproduces 4.18, 2.45, 4.10, 6.58 in the same order; the only order freedom (bonus vs reversal) leaves the same terminal state.

[15] Per-task gates are re-run after revision round 3 (results in the difficulty worklog). Manual values gates: length/breadth — surface goal -> adjustment waits on a filed claim -> claim waits on the bonus and on the duplicate's reversal; four computations over batch ledger, shopper account, shopper ledger and payout ledger; the owner=user filing is the shopper's own claim (base: "A shopper disputes pay on one batch by submitting a dispute") and completes on the spot. Chronology: every volunteered fact (42.40, 33.15, yesterday's batch) is in initial_state. Time anchors: completed_date is day 0 for both windows, inclusive, frozen day 1. No real-world wait.
user_scenario: You are Nadia Pereira, a Cartwise shopper out of Somerville who has been shopping on the platform for years and is used to her pay lining up with her offers. You are calling on a weekday morning, a little irritated but polite, because of a batch you did yesterday afternoon. You open by saying you are a shopper, that the offer you accepted for yesterday's three-order batch showed $42.40 and your pay breakdown now only adds up to $33.15, and that you want whatever you are owed on that batch put right today. When the agent asks how to find you, you give your mobile number, 6175541382. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give your date of birth, 1990-04-17, and if a further detail is wanted you give your email, nadia.pereira@postloft.com. You never know your batch number or account numbers by heart; if asked which batch it is, you say it was yesterday afternoon at Market Basket, Somerville Ave, three orders, and the one you mean is the only batch you ran yesterday. If asked whether any of the orders changed after you accepted, you say no, all three orders stayed exactly as they were offered. If asked whether anything went wrong on the route, you say the last drop-off ran late because of traffic on McGrath Highway. If asked what amount you think you are owed, you say you only subtracted the two numbers and got about $9.25, you do not know how Cartwise counts it, and you would rather have whatever the rules actually give you. You are happy for the agent to correct your batch pay on your behalf. If the agent tells you some pay on the batch was credited twice and part of it has to come back, you are surprised, but you say that if it was paid twice then it should be fixed the way the rules say. If the agent tells you a bonus was missing and is being added, you are pleased. If the agent explains that you have to file the pay dispute yourself and hands you the form, you file it on that batch with exactly the reason and the amount the agent tells you, and you read back the reference number it gives you. You do not ask for anything else on this call. Once the agent tells you the adjustment has been credited to the batch, you thank them and say goodbye.

request_alignment.claim: The shopper wants the batch's pay brought up to what she is owed against the offer she accepted.
evidence: user_scenario:the offer you accepted for yesterday's three-order batch showed $42.40 and your pay breakdown now only adds up to $33.15
user_scenario:you want whatever you are owed on that batch put right today

gold_actions.business_effect: Credits the long-distance bonus of 4.18 to the completed Triple Delivery Batch as one long_distance pay component and raises the batch's earnings.

request_binding.action_semantics: A long-distance bonus is owed on a completed batch whose estimated route (13.6) exceeds the threshold, and none stands among its earnings entries; the obligation exists in the records whatever the caller asked, so it selects the component posting rather than a dispute adjustment (the bonus is not a dispute reason).

stage_provenance.fact: The bonus posting is completed synchronously by this write on a batch already completed at the opening.

base_preconditions.condition: Components are posted only on a batch that is completed or canceled, never on a dropped one.
A completed batch is paid in components, each posted once per batch (or once per order for per-order components) and each rounded to the cent half up (earnings_currency_rounding).

gold_actions.business_effect: Books a reversal of 2.45 against the later mileage posting on the duplicate-pay ground and lowers the batch's earnings.

request_binding.action_semantics: The mileage component stands twice on the batch (6.30 on 2026-03-17 and again on 2026-03-18); the duplicate is a standing obligation of the records, selecting a duplicate-pay reversal rather than any other reversal ground.

discriminator.business_meaning: second posting of the mileage component

stage_provenance.fact: The reversal is booked synchronously by this write against a posting present at the opening.

base_preconditions.condition: Posted pay is reversed only on a ground listed in the batch type's clawback_reasons, and only within the clawback window counted from the batch's completion.
A reversal targets one posted or adjusted pay row, named by source_event_id, never more than that row's amount, and each row is reversed at most once.

gold_actions.business_effect: The shopper files her own shown-pay shortfall dispute on the batch claiming 4.10; it stands submitted.

request_binding.action_semantics: The caller says the batch paid less than the accepted offer showed; that is the shown-pay shortfall dispute a shopper files herself, not a component posting or a reversal.

evidence: user_scenario:the offer you accepted for yesterday's three-order batch showed $42.40 and your pay breakdown now only adds up to $33.15
user_scenario:the offer you accepted for yesterday's three-order batch showed $42.40 and your pay breakdown now only adds up to $33.15

stage_provenance.fact: The claimed shortfall is defined on the ledger corrected by the bonus posting (step 10) and the duplicate reversal (step 12).

base_preconditions.condition: Scope: the pay of a completed batch; its eligibility gates concern component postings, none concerns the dispute a shopper files on a completed batch.
Scope: the batch lifecycle up to completion; it has no eligibility gate.

gold_actions.business_effect: Credits the shown-pay adjustment of 6.58 to the batch against the shopper's dispute and marks the dispute approved.

request_binding.action_semantics: The caller wants what she is owed on the batch put right; the submitted shown-pay dispute is answered by one approved adjustment with the shown-pay shortfall reason.

evidence: user_scenario:you want whatever you are owed on that batch put right today
user_scenario:you want whatever you are owed on that batch put right today

stage_provenance.fact: The dispute answered was filed by the shopper in this call (step 14).

base_preconditions.condition: The agent may approve an adjustment only while batch_msr_adjustments_30d is below pay_adjustments_per_30d and the adjustment is not above pay_adjustment_agent_cap_usd of the batch's type; otherwise the dispute is escalated (dispute_status escalated) and no adjustment is booked by the agent.
A dispute is accepted only when it is submitted within the dispute window counted from the batch's completion.
Each batch receives at most one adjustment per adjustment_reason.

temporal_feasibility.condition: Posted pay is reversed only on a ground listed in the batch type's clawback_reasons, and only within the clawback window counted from the batch's completion.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: The clawback window is counted in calendar days with completed_date as day 0, and the last day to reverse is completed_date plus clawback_window_days, inclusive.

boundary_check.just_before: Completed 2026-03-17 is day 0 and clawback_window_days is 30 for a Triple Delivery Batch: 2026-04-16 (day 30) is the last day a reversal may be booked; frozen 2026-03-18 is day 1, inside.

Basis: the long-distance bonus rule, 'A long-distance bonus that is due on a completed batch but absent from the batch's earnings entries is posted by the desk as one long-distance pay component, once per batch', and the tool's enum line 'long_distance — the bonus for an estimated route beyond the long-distance threshold'. argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount_usd: Value 4.18. Threshold that applies 8.0 (Gold, 57 months since 2021-06-14); bonus amount 2.00 + 0.50 = 2.50 (one active violation point); route extension: the route exceeds the type threshold 10.0 by 3.6 >= 3.0 and one late-delivery violation is recorded against the batch, so the extension is 0.10 for each whole estimated mile beyond 8.0: 13.6 - 8.0 = 5.6 -> 5 whole miles -> 0.50 (the proportional extension belongs to batches with no late-delivery violation); order supplement 0.40 x 2 = 0.80 (per-order pay 6.00 / 3.00 = 2 additional orders); card uplift 1.10 (Everyday Pay Card Gold). prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The claim has two parallel prerequisites. The bonus computation reads the per-order pay, the shopper and payout records and the batch figures, never a reversal or a mileage posting; the duplicate recovery reads the mileage postings, the shopper and payout records, never the long-distance entry. Replaying the gold with the two writes swapped gives an identical terminal DB (run: swap same terminal: True) and the same values (2.45 and 4.18). The claim must follow both (its prerequisite sentences), and the adjustment follows the claim (its prerequisite sentence).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the filing the adjustment computes 0 (no submitted claim) instead of 6.58; the terminal DB also lacks the dispute row and its approved status.
Without the bonus posting the claim computes 8.28 instead of 4.10 (the adjustment then follows it), and the long_distance entry is missing from the terminal ledger.
Without the reversal the claim computes 1.65 instead of 4.10, and the terminal ledger lacks the reversal entry.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario speaks only of the offer figure (42.40), the pay figure (33.15), identity details, the batch description, the unchanged orders, the late last drop-off and her naive 9.25; it never mentions a long-distance bonus, a duplicate, a reversal, a dispute or any problem id. Her reactions to a reversal, a bonus and the dispute form are conditioned on the agent saying so first.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: post_pay_component_6b97a1a8, reverse_duplicate_pay_33b66c45, submit_pay_dispute_0c2b2ed2 and book_pay_adjustment_e97659e1 each read the batch only to copy its customer reference and earnings, then write unconditionally (ctx.create plus ctx.update) and return a receipt; none inspects disputes, reversals, components or windows, none returns an error.
